pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome back letter from the Headteacher - School News & Updates - Kensington Avenue Primary School
pageCache.text:
Welcome back letter from the Headteacher
New Headteacher Mr Peter Killip warmly welcomes families to the new school year, expressing his gratitude for the community's warm reception while setting out key safety updates, site improvements, and new staff appointments.
Key Highlights & Important Announcements
Headteacher's Vision: Mr Killip shares his pride in joining Kensington Avenue Primary School and challenges every pupil to make a simple promise: to try their best every day
KS2 Dismissal Arrangements: All Key Stage 2 pupils will now be dismissed directly from the Lower Playground. Older pupils are no longer permitted to collect younger siblings on the school site
Independent Travel Policy: Independent travel to and from school is strictly restricted to Year 6 pupils only, subject to a signed permission form completed via the school office.
Site & Building Upgrades: Extensive work was completed over the summer break to boost site safety and security, with further enhancements planned in the coming months.
New Staff Members: KAPS extends a warm welcome to Mrs Wingate (Year 1), Mrs Morris-Moore (Year 2), Miss Ali (Year 3), Miss Richards (Year 4), and Mr Matthews (Assistant Headteacher).
Community Engagement: Mr Killip will be present at the school gates during morning arrival and afternoon dismissal to meet and speak with parents and carers.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from the Headteacher - Kensington Avenue Primary School
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Headteacher
Welcome to Kensington Avenue Primary School, a community school for children aged 2 to 11 and a proud member of Wandle Learning Trust.
At Kensington Avenue, we believe that every child deserves to feel safe, valued and a genuine sense of belonging. Positive relationships are at the heart of everything we do because we know that children thrive when they feel known, understood and cared for. We see education as a partnership and, by working closely with families, we help every child to flourish both academically and personally.
We are ambitious for all our children. Our curriculum is designed to inspire curiosity, broaden horizons and develop the knowledge and skills children need for success in the future. We want every child to see themselves reflected in their learning while also gaining an understanding of the wider world beyond their immediate experience. Through a rich range of learning opportunities, we nurture confident, resilient and independent learners who are ready to make a positive contribution to society.
Alongside our high ambitions for learning, we are equally committed to ensuring that every child feels a strong sense of belonging within our school community.
Inclusion is a fundamental part of who we are. We want every child to know that they belong at Kensington Avenue. We celebrate diversity, value individuality and work closely with families to ensure that children feel safe, understood and supported throughout their time with us. By building strong relationships and providing the right support at the right time, we help children develop confidence, independence and a belief in their own potential.
We are proud to have a specialist ASD Resource Base that is fully integrated into school life and forms an important part of our school family.
Beyond the classroom, children benefit from a wide range of experiences that enrich their learning and support their personal development. Our beautiful grounds provide opportunities for learning, exploration and play, while partnerships with organisations such as St Oswald's Church, Palace for Life Foundation and Croydon Sports Partnership help broaden children's experiences, develop new interests and strengthen their connection with the local community.
Most importantly, Kensington Avenue is a place where children are happy, feel they belong and are encouraged to become the very best version of themselves. We want every child to leave us with wonderful memories, strong values and the knowledge, skills and confidence to succeed in the next stage of their education and beyond.
I hope our website gives you a flavour of life at Kensington Avenue Primary School, but there is no substitute for seeing our community in action. We would be delighted to welcome you for a visit and show you what makes our school such a special place to learn and grow.
We look forward to meeting you.
In This Section
Headteacher Mr P Killip

pageCache.pageTitle: Family School Partnership - Kensington Avenue Primary School
pageCache.text:
Family School Partnership
Mrs. P Bhambra is our Family Support Worker, and her role at Kensington Avenue Primary School is to provide support, advice, and information to families within our school community. She is here to help with any concerns you may have regarding your child, their behaviour, wellbeing, or if you simply need someone to talk to.
Advice and support provided by Mrs. Bhambra is confidential, although concerns related to the safeguarding of children will always be addressed in line with the school's Safeguarding and Child Protection Policies. While she may not have all the answers, she will work with you to find the right solutions.
Support for children includes:
Support for families includes:
Supporting Pupil Premium pupils
Promoting good attendance and punctuality
Encouraging self-esteem and confidence
Promoting positive behaviour and attitudes toward learning
Providing information and signposting to local services
Assisting with completing paperwork and forms

pageCache.pageTitle: KAPS Newsletter - 11.09.2026 - School News & Updates - Kensington Avenue Primary School
pageCache.text:
KAPS Newsletter - 11.09.2026
Kensington Avenue Primary School has wrapped up a successful first full week of the autumn term, celebrating strong pupil engagement, site upgrades, and exciting new learning initiatives.
Headteacher’s Welcome & Attendance Raffle: Mr. Killip reflected on a fantastic start to the year, noting pupils' enthusiasm and impressive reasoning skills in mathematics. Starting next week, every child achieving 100% weekly attendance will enter a raffle to win a brand-new book.
Reception Welcome: New Reception pupils settled into school life, creating self-portraits for their "Me and My Community" topic, while parents were welcomed with first-week treats.
Classroom Spotlight: Practical learning was underway across all year groups—from Year 3 crafting moving skeletons in science to Year 4 and Year 5 beginning recorder and clarinet music lessons.
Hot Chocolate Friday: The first Hot Chocolate Friday celebrated a nominated group of pupils who went above and beyond in their efforts.
Some Upcoming Events
Meet the Teacher Sessions: Monday, 14th September – Friday, 18th September.
Year 6 SATs & Residential Meeting: Thursday, 17th September (3:30 PM – 4:30 PM).
Open Morning: Friday, 25th September (9:15 AM – 10:00 AM).
Parent Workshops: Weekly Tuesday morning crochet and knitting workshops return at 9:00 AM.

pageCache.pageTitle: KAPS Newsletter - 25.09.2026 - School News & Updates - Kensington Avenue Primary School
pageCache.text:
KAPS Newsletter - 25.09.2026
Headteacher Mr Killip reflects on pupil resilience, attendance awards, and increasing opportunities for family involvement, alongside key diary dates and rich classroom updates across all year groups.
Headteacher's Updates & Pupil Recognition
Attendance HERO Campaign: Pupils achieving 100% attendance each week are entered into a raffle, with three winners chosen to take home a brand-new book.
Open Community Vision: The school is actively opening its doors to welcome prospective and current parents, carers, and visiting educational colleagues.
Key Diary Dates
Secondary School Application Workshop: Thursday 1st October, 9:00am–11:00am.
PTA Coffee Morning: Monday 5th October, 9:00am–10:30am.
KAPS Book Fair: Monday 5th October – Friday 9th October (3:15pm–4:00pm in the KS2 Hall).
Harvest Festival Donations: Tuesday 6th October (collecting non-perishable goods for Beulah Food Bank).
Open Morning & School Photographs: Friday 9th October (Open Morning 9:15am–10:00am; photo sessions held all day).
PTA Annual General Meeting (AGM): Tuesday 13th October at 4:00pm.
Classroom & Curriculum Spotlights
Early Years: Nursery pupils are settling into outdoor learning and sensory play, while Reception explored family careers after reading My Mum is a Firefighter.
Key Stage 1: Year 1 created "messy maps" and model aerial views. Year 2 explored texture artwork, cookery (baking cookies in Poppy Class), and the importance of bedtime routines in PSHE.
Lower Key Stage 2: Year 3 studied bodily cues for emotions and practised observational drawing. Year 4 conducted hands-on science projects, modelling dental structures with playdough and testing toothbrush bristle effectiveness.
Upper Key Stage 2: Year 5 investigated light properties (transparent, translucent, opaque) and calming meditation techniques. Year 6 created online safety posters as "Web Wise Wizards" and focused on clear mathematical reasoning.
Community & Administrative Notices
Free School Meals (FSM): Families are urged to check eligibility via the school website's checker tool to access school meal funding and holiday supermarket vouchers.
Friends of KAPS (PTA): Parents and carers are invited to join fundraising efforts and follow the PTA on Instagram (@friendsofkaps).
